#en:
Did not even mean to be on this rock past one cycle. In, hand off routes, out. That was the plan.

Instead I am sitting in a buzzing metal box with scorched paint, listening to recycled air wheeze and watching that UC hull spin lazy on the scopes. The big one, half-dead, like somebody took a bite out of its side and forgot to finish the meal. That is where I traced the pattern to in the end. Not to some pirate den or Neon backroom, but to a ship that used to write the patrols everyone else obeyed.

The smugglers keep arguing about how it went down. Some say she sold the corridor twice, once to the Fleet, once to SysDef, let them smash together for the payout. Others swear she warned the UC and hung the pirates out to dry. Same story, different villain, and nobody really wants to chase the details in case the truth ruins a good rumor or points back at their own crew.

What I know is simpler. Every ghost run I arranged for her, every too-perfect window that dropped us between sensor sweeps, left a fingerprint in our logs and theirs. I followed those smudges through GalBank insurance packets, through freighters that arrived too early with too much fuel left, through manifests that did not balance. All the stray timings line up on that crippled SysDef ship out there. Whatever she did to bend their routes, the record of it is still in that carcass, waiting for someone desperate or stubborn enough to go pull it loose.
zh:
我本没打算在这块岩石上待过一整个周期。进来，交接航线，出去。那就是计划。

结果我却坐在一只漆面烧焦、嗡嗡作响的铁盒子里，听着再循环空气喘息，看着那具联殖船壳在示波器上懒洋洋地旋转。那具大家伙，半死不活，像有人从它侧面咬了一口就忘了吃完。我最终把图案追到了那里。不是某个海盗窝，也不是霓虹城的密室，而是一艘曾经写下其他所有人都得遵守的巡逻表的飞船。

走私贩们还在为事情是怎么败露的争论不休。有人说她把那条走廊卖了两次，一次卖给舰队，一次卖给星防队，让他们撞在一起好拿报酬。另一些人赌咒说她警告了联殖，把海盗晾在一边。同一个故事，不同的反派，而没人真想去追细节，生怕真相毁了一则好传言，或者指回自己的船员身上。

我知道的更简单。我为她安排的每一次幽灵航次，每一个把我们丢进传感器扫描之间的完美时窗，都在我们的日志和他们的日志里留下了一枚指纹。我顺着那些污迹穿过盖尔银行的保险数据包，穿过来得太早、燃料剩得太多的货船，穿过对不上账的清单。所有那些游离的时序都排在外面那艘残废的星防队飞船上。不管她做了什么去掰弯他们的航线，记录还留在那具残骸里，等着哪个够绝望或够固执的人去把它拉出来。

#en:
I used to think there was no such thing as a haunted jump, just bad maintenance and worse captains.

Then I started hauling out of Gagarin more regularly, and the stories stopped being funny. Same kind of wrecks drifting back in, same scorch marks around the grav housing, and everyone swearing they had followed approved plots. Insurance blamed "operator error" every time, stamped, filed, forgotten. Funny how error keeps drawing the same curve across different ships.

The first time I saw it myself was last year, somewhere between Polvo and a nowhere mining rock. Nav threw a fit, all red bands and warning tones, then suddenly the display calmed down and smoothed into a new course like nothing had happened. ETA shaved by twenty minutes. My copilot whooped, said we had luck on our side. My stomach did not agree.

I pulled the raw telemetry later. Hidden in the noise were those neat little adjustments, burn durations that lined up on prime numbers, angles nudged just off what any auto-plotter would pick. It looked hand-drawn, like somebody had reached into the system and guided us past the worst of the debris while the machine thought it was still in charge.

For a while I told myself it was a software quirk nobody had patched. But the more logs I collected, the more clear it got: someone was carving secret lanes through the dark, and we had been following their handwriting for a long time before anyone bothered to notice.
zh:
我以前以为不存在闹鬼的跃迁，只有糟糕的维护和更糟的船长。

后来我开始更频繁地从加加林出航，那些故事就不再好笑了。同样是那类残骸漂回来，重力舱周围是同样的烧痕，而人人都赌咒说自己按批准的航路图走的。保险公司每次都说"操作员失误"，盖章、归档、遗忘。有趣的是，"失误"如何在不同的飞船上画出同一条曲线。

我第一次亲眼见到是去年，在波尔沃和一块无名采矿岩石之间的某处。导航大发脾气，全是红色带和警告音，然后显示忽然平静下来，顺进一条新航线，像什么都没发生。预计抵达时间少了二十分钟。我的副驾驶欢呼，说我们运气好。我的胃不同意。

后来我调出了原始遥测。藏在噪声里的，是那些整齐的小调整——燃烧时长排成质数，角度被拨得刚好偏离任何自动标绘器会选的值。它看起来像手绘的，像有人伸进系统，引导我们穿过最糟的碎片，而机器还以为仍是自己在掌舵。

有一阵子我告诉自己，那是个没人修补的软件怪癖。可我收集的日志越多，就越清楚：有人在黑暗中凿出秘密航道，而我们已经沿着他们的笔迹走了很久，很久之后才有人费心去注意。

#en:
There is still coffee dried into the grooves of the console, and I catch myself wondering whose mug it was before remembering how that ends. They tell us in training that Vanguard ships do not just disappear; every jump is logged, every variance audited. Someone forgot to tell this hull. We picked up the distress whisper by accident, a slurred echo buried under fuel reports from a quiet depot that should never have routed to my station. The ID read Vanguard, then blinked out as if embarrassed.

I have been cross-checking traffic for two days. The scout should have been on a patrol arc near a debris corridor. Instead, its last confirmed path threads neatly through a cluster of wrecks all marked with the same suspiciously efficient clearances. Dock logs at that dusty fuel stop did not match the tank levels on outgoing ships, and the clerk insisted their system just "rounded up." Somebody mis-typed a timestamp, someone else filed the wrong route, and in the gaps between those little errors, an entire crew dropped off the board.

Now I am sitting in their dead ship, listening to the hull creak, watching half-burned nav data redraw the same elegant curves over and over. Whatever is buried on this vessel will not just explain what happened here. It will tell me who has been quietly steering us all this time, and why every time a story about those perfect routes reaches my desk, the details never line up quite the same way twice.
zh:
控制台的沟槽里还干着咖啡渍，我会不由自主地想那是谁的杯子，然后想起那会怎么结束。训练时他们告诉我们，先锋队的飞船不会就这么消失；每一次跃迁都有记录，每一处偏差都被审计。有人忘了告诉这具船壳。我们是偶然截获到那声求救低语的——一段含糊的回响，埋在来自一座安静补给站的燃料报告底下，而那座补给站本不该路由到我的站点。ID 显示是先锋队，然后像难为情一样眨一下就熄了。

我这两天一直在交叉核对交通。那艘侦察艇本该在一处碎片走廊附近的巡逻弧线上。可它最后确认的路径，却整齐地穿过一簇残骸，全都带着同样可疑地"高效"的放行许可。那座尘土飞扬的补给站的码头日志与出港飞船的油罐液位对不上，而那文员坚称他们的系统只是"向上取整"了。有人打错了一个时间戳，另一个人归错了航线，而在那些小错误之间的缝隙里，一整队船员从板上消失了。

此刻我坐在他们死去的飞船里，听着船体吱嘎作响，看着半烧毁的导航数据一遍遍重绘同样优雅的曲线。这艘船上埋着的东西，不只解释这里发生了什么。它会告诉我，是谁一直在悄悄为我们所有人掌舵；以及为什么每次关于那些完美航线的故事传到我桌上时，细节从来不会两次吻合得一模一样。

#en:
I am recording this in the mess, lights dimmed, engines barely a hum through the hull. The banners on the bulkhead still carry the old slogans about duty and vigilance, but nobody repeats them out loud anymore. Out here, you learn that saying the wrong thing travels faster than any ship, and someone always has a reason to file it away.

Before we launched, I spent a night in Neon, up in one of the quieter lounges where the music does not quite drown out the deals. Heard a hauler talk about a phantom in the traffic nets, some ex-controller picking favorites in the lanes. People laughed, then checked their route clearances twice before boarding.

Now I am on this SysDef wreck, helmet lamp cutting across frozen consoles and bodies that died doing what the pamphlets called "essential work." The navigation logs are jagged, overwritten in places by something that does not look standard issue. Whoever rode this ship into silence got close to something they were not supposed to see, and every gap on these drives feels less like a malfunction and more like a warning to keep my own thoughts clipped and tidy.

The more I dig, the more the stories line up: captains in Neon muttering about lucky detours, a tech in The Well selling copies of hearings that never happened, a dead hauler from HopeTown whose "priority advisory" led straight into a killzone. Different systems, same invisible hand tracing the same sharp curve through the void.
zh:
我在食堂里录下这些，灯光调暗，引擎透过船体只剩一点微弱的嗡鸣。舱壁上的横幅还挂着关于职责与警觉的老口号，可再没人把它们念出声。在这外面，你会明白说错话传得比任何飞船都快，而总有人有理由把它归档留底。

我们出发前，我在霓虹城待了一晚，在一间音乐盖不太住交易的安静酒廊里。听到一个运货船员谈起交通网里的幽灵，某个前管制员在航道上挑三拣四地偏心。人们笑了，然后在登船前把航线许可核对了两次。

如今我在这具星防队残骸上，头盔灯扫过冻结的控制台，和那些在宣传册称之为"必要工作"中死去的人。导航日志支离破碎，有些地方被某种看起来不像标准配发的东西覆盖过。把这条船开进沉寂的人，靠近了他们本不该看见的东西；而每一处驱动上的空白，都越来越不像故障，而更像一句警告——叫我把自己的念头也修剪得干净利落。

我挖得越深，那些故事就越对上：霓虹城的船长们嘟囔着幸运的绕行，深井区的一个技工在兜售从未发生过的听证会副本，一个来自希望镇的死货船船员，其"优先咨询"直通一片杀伤区。不同的星系，同一只看不见的手，在虚空中描出同一条锐利的曲线。

#en:
I am recording this because I keep hearing the same story in different mouths, and out here with PX-9199 dead in the water, stories are all that move.

Dock 17 was the first time I heard her called by that callsign. Some Vanguard vet in a scuffed flight jacket, nursing a TerraBrew like it was the last decent thing left in the galaxy, said she threaded a convoy through a Crimson net without firing a shot. Two days later, in a corner booth on Neon, a Ryujin clerk swore she sold their analysts drift data that did not match any known jump physics. Same name, different angle. Hero. Traitor. Ghost.

Now I am standing in a darkened CIC, watching PX-9199's last jump log smear into static right where the squadron should have synced. That gap everyone pretends is a sensor error has the same taste as those bar stories, the same shape. Too clean to be chance, too ugly to be official. They say she walked away from this kind of ship when the record turned on her. They say command buried the truth to keep the lanes calm.

What gets me is how the tale keeps improving itself every time it is told, drifting from rumor to inevitability. A pilot who knows the places drives slip. A wing that vanished. A name that shows up wherever the math stops adding up. I used to file it with spacer superstition. Looking at this wreck, listening to its broken heart try to beat, I am starting to think the story has been circling the real coordinates all along.
zh:
我录下这个，因为我不断从不同的嘴里听到同一个故事；而在这外面，PX-9199 死在水里，能动的只有故事。

17 号泊位是我第一次听到别人用那个呼号叫她。一个穿着磨旧飞行夹克的先锋队老兵，捧着一杯地球酿酒像那是银河里仅剩的像样东西，说她不发一枪就把一支运输队穿过了深红舰队的网。两天后，在霓虹城一个角落卡座里，一个龙神文员赌咒说她卖给他们的分析师一些不符合任何已知跃迁物理的漂移数据。同一个名字，不同的角度。英雄。叛徒。幽灵。

如今我站在一间变暗的作战信息中心里，看着 PX-9199 的最后一份跃迁日志恰好在本该与中队同步的地方糊成静电。人人都假装是传感器故障的那道缺口，尝起来和那些酒吧故事一个味道，形状也一样。太干净，不像偶然；太丑陋，不像官方。他们说，当纪录开始对她不利时，她离开了这类飞船。他们说，指挥部为了保持航道平静，把真相埋了。

让我在意的是，这故事每被讲一次就自我完善一次，从传言漂向必然。一个知道驱动会打滑之处的飞行员。一支消失的僚机编队。一个在算式加不起来的地方就出现的名字。我以前把它和太空人的迷信归在一起。看着这具残骸，听着它破碎的心试图跳动，我开始觉得这故事一直在绕着真实的坐标转。

#en:
I am filing this as a personal log because the official channel keeps timing out and, if I am honest, I do not really want anyone higher up reading it.

We have been shadowing these broken flight paths for three weeks now. First that empty rock where someone ditched a crate of nav slates like they were radioactive, then the busted relay with its guts rearranged so no one could tell where anything actually went. Now this little Navy scout, cut adrift in a place no one has business being, its course history knotted up in patterns that make my head hurt.

The weird part is how ordinary everyone treated it at first. Just another recovery op, just another derelict with a nice clean ID and a maintenance backlog we could bill for. The last team that touched these routes logged their work, signed off, and went home. They did not wait around to see why the same signature kept cropping up at abandoned farms and half-built outposts, or ask why every "optimized" vector seemed to pass close to the same dark patch of sky.

I keep replaying their notes, hearing how casual they sound. They tugged on a loose thread, filed their reports, and transferred to safer contracts. The mess they left behind has teeth. Standing on this dead ship, listening to the hull pop and settle, I cannot shake the feeling that all of us have been moving data and metal for someone else's idea of mercy, and we walked away long before we understood what we helped build.
zh:
我把这份归为个人日志，因为官方频道老是超时；而且说实话，我其实不太想让上面任何人读到它。

我们已经追踪这些破碎的飞行路径三周了。先是那块空岩石，有人像扔放射性物质一样把一箱导航数据板丢在那儿；然后是那座内脏被重新摆弄过的坏中继站，让人看不出任何东西究竟去了哪儿。现在又是这艘小小的海军侦察艇，被抛弃在没人该去的地方，它的航向历史被打成让我头疼的结。

古怪的是，起初所有人都把它当成平常事。不过是又一次回收行动，又一具带着漂亮干净 ID、还有维护积压可以开账单的弃船。上一支处理这些航线的队伍记录了工作、签了字，然后回家了。他们没有多留下来看看为什么同一个特征不断出现在废弃农场和半建成的前哨站，也没问为什么每一条"优化"矢量似乎都经过同一片黑暗天空。

我不断重放他们的笔记，听他们说得多么随意。他们扯了一根松线头，提交了报告，然后调去接更安全的合同。他们留下的那摊乱子会咬人。站在这艘死船上，听着船体砰砰作响、慢慢沉降，我怎么也甩不掉一个感觉：我们所有人都在为别人对"仁慈"的构想搬运数据和金属，而我们在弄懂自己帮建了什么之前，早就走开了。

#en:
I told myself I'd go back out there.

First time I saw the place was by accident, dropping cargo two valleys over. The foreman pointed it out like you'd point at an old scar, said the owners left in the night when the bank called in the note. What stuck with me wasn't the house, it was the glow on the metering panel. Dead farm, live power. Someone still feeding it credits.

I swung by once on the way home. Stayed in orbit, zoomed in with the scope. Saw the black-and-white armor at the doors, rifles cradled but not relaxed, a generator thumping steady in the yard. Mercenaries do not babysit empty soil for free. I logged the coordinates, marked it "follow-up" in my slate.

That was three months and too many runs ago. Every time I line up a free day, something gets in the way: late shipment, pirate scare, a "random" inspection that feels a little too targeted. Like the universe or the people who pay to shape it want that note on my slate to stay unfinished.

What bothers me is how the stories line up. A bar on Akila where they talk about a ranch that woke up debt-free. A LIST broadcast where a settler thanks an unnamed "friend in the system." Dockworkers humming that same tune about some fixer who can make numbers disappear. Someone out there pulled this farm back from the brink on paper, then let the land rot and paid Uniform Blackguard to keep everyone away.

Feels like I wasn't the only one who meant to loop back and never did.
zh:
我告诉自己我会回到那儿去。

我第一次看到那地方是偶然——在两条山谷外卸货。那工头像指一道旧疤一样指了指它，说银行来催债的那个夜里，主人就悄悄走了。让我记住的不是那栋房子，而是计量面板上的光。死掉的农场，活着的电力。还有人一直在往里喂信用币。

回家的路上我绕过去看过一次。留在轨道上，用镜头拉近。看见门口那身黑白装甲，步枪端着却不放松，院子里一台发电机稳定地砰砰作响。雇佣兵不会白给人看守空土。我记下坐标，在我的数据板上标成"待跟进"。

那是三个月和无数趟航次之前了。每次我排出一个空闲的日子，就有事挡道：迟到的货运、海盗的惊扰、一次感觉有点太有针对性的"随机"检查。像宇宙，或者那些花钱塑造宇宙的人，想让我数据板上那条备注一直完不成。

让我不安的是那些故事怎么对得上。阿基拉一间酒吧里，人们谈论一座一觉醒来就免了债的牧场。一期独立盟广播里，一个定居者感谢一位不具名的"体制里的朋友"。码头工哼着同样的调子，说某个能让数字消失的调停人。外面有人在纸面上把这座农场从悬崖边拉了回来，然后任由土地烂掉，还花钱雇来"统一黑卫"把所有人挡开。

感觉像我不是唯一一个本打算回来、却再没回来的人。
